item.title: Infrastructure as Code Tools
item.description: If you’re involved in DevOps, you should be acquainted with Infrastructure as Code (IaC). IaC allows you to write code to define, deploy, update, and dismantle IT infrastructure, rather than manually performing these tasks. There are numerous tools designed to aid in IaC. These can be grouped into five categories: Ad hoc scripts Configuration management tools Server templating tools Orchestration tools Provisioning tools Ad hoc scripts Ad hoc scripts are a straightforward method for automating tasks or configuring tools.

item.title: Learning about Kubernetes
item.description: Recently I read a very good overview of Kubernetes architecture by Julia Evans. The 5 most important components in Kubernetes are: etcd the API server the scheduler kubelets on every node the controller manager etcd is the central place where other components check what they have to do and it also stores the states of other components. The API server is the interface to send what have to do into etcd.

item.title: The Golang Web Frameworks for Beginner
item.description: There are many web frameworks in Golang. As I know, there are at least 11 web frameworks that the Golang developers are frequently using for their projects. For example, Gin, Beego, Kit, Echo, FastHttp, Fiber, Mux, Kratos, Httprouter, Revel, Go-zero, Martini, and etc. For beginners, the abundance of choices makes them difficult to decide which web framework to use. To help solve this problem, I would suggest the beginners first learn Gin web framework, and then Beego web frameworks.
